paper.title: AutoDroid: LLM-powered Task Automation in Android
paper.central_claim: AutoDroid is a mobile task automation system that handles arbitrary tasks on any Android application without manual effort by combining LLM commonsense with app-specific knowledge obtained through automated dynamic analysis (functionality-aware UI prompting, exploration-based memory injection, multi-granularity query optimization); reported 90.9% action accuracy and 71.3% task completion, +36.4% and +39.7% over GPT-4-powered baselines. Scope as measured: DroidTask, 158 tasks over 13 F-Droid apps, scored offline against one human-annotated trace per task.

provenance.session_receipt_note: worker subagent has no exposed session id or receipt in its context; null by design
provenance.contamination: none observed: did not open the other seat, Opus aggregate, old scores, old Reel, archive/ or other batches

evidence.quote: The results demonstrated that AutoDroid is able to precisely generate actions with an accuracy of 90.9%, and complete tasks with a success rate of 71.3%, outperforming the GPT-4-powered baselines by 36.4% and 39.7%.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated central quantitative claim.

evidence.quote: (ii) Completion Rate : The probability of completing all the actions in one sequence correctly
evidence.support_explanation: The reported "success rate" is trace-matching completion, not live task success.

evidence.quote: The actual completion rate in the real-system can be higher than the reported results, but we do not include real-system results since determining task completion can be ambiguous.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state that no live-execution result is reported.

evidence.quote: Annotators may not be able to exhaustively list all the possible ways to complete a task, and if the agent attempts a different approach than what the annotators specified, it may be deemed incorrect.
evidence.support_explanation: Single annotated trace gives false negatives; metric validity limit.
Column order Rand, Sim, MG, then LLM-F/AutoDroid for Vicuna-7B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4: GPT-4 LLM-F 54.5% vs AutoDroid 90.9%.
LLM-framework scores 0 on the completion-judgement action for both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, so part of the overall action-accuracy gap is the baseline never emitting "complete".
Click accuracy alone also moves (GPT-4: 65.4% to 91.2%), so the gap is not only the completion action.

evidence.quote: AutoDroid outperforms baseline by 40.5%, 26.4%, and 39.7% for Vicuna-7B, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Completion-rate gains; the same section says the completion-determination step is excluded from this comparison.

evidence.quote: AutoDroid prunes and merges UI elements, which reduces the action space (from 36.4 to 13.2 choices per GUI state on average).
evidence.support_explanation: Representation change alone shrinks the choice set 2.8x, a plausible competing explanation for gains.

evidence.quote: We can observe that the improvement in overall completion rate is much higher than the improvement in single-step accuracy.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory on/off result is only given qualitatively in text (Figure 8 bars not extractable).

evidence.quote: Metric Original AutoDroid No Mo No CoT No Mo&CoT Action 11.3% 57.7% 51.9% 20.6% 51.9% Completion 0.6% 41.1% 29.8% 0.6% 31.6%
evidence.support_explanation: Vicuna-7B fine-tuning ablation; CoT only matters once MoTiF data is mixed in (No Mo&CoT 51.9% equals No Mo 51.9%).

evidence.quote: AutoDroid determines the importance of a UI element in the app memory based on the similarity between its simulated task and the current user task.
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval/selection rule for memory injection (embedding cosine top-k).

evidence.quote: AutoDroid explores the app by randomly clicking buttons on the screen and records the result in a UI Transition Graph (UTG) memory
evidence.support_explanation: Memory is built by random exploration of the same apps later used for tasks.

evidence.quote: DroidTask consists of 158 high-level tasks extracted from 13 popular apps.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation scope and denominator.

evidence.quote: Agents can actively interact with the environment during the offline stage, gathering information about the apps and recording UTGs.
evidence.support_explanation: Offline exploration of the benchmark apps is part of the protocol; no held-out apps.

evidence.quote: includes only visible leaf nodes in the UI tree, and contains 625.3 tokens within each prompt on average. AutoDroid merges functionally equivalent nodes in the UI tree and further simplifies the expression of properties, reducing the token count by nearly half (339.0 on average).
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline vs AutoDroid prompt tokens.

evidence.quote: Our shortcuts correctly guide LLMs in 75% of cases.
evidence.support_explanation: Shortcut rule is wrong a quarter of the time; the authors say the LLM then recovers.

evidence.quote: For every app, it takes about 0.5-1 hour to generate the UI Transition Graph (UTG)
evidence.support_explanation: Offline cost per app.

evidence.quote: The temperature of the LLMs is set to a lower value of 0.25 to encourage creativity while preventing it from being overly random.
evidence.support_explanation: Sampling setting; no repeated runs reported.

evidence.quote: increasing the temperature to 0.7 boosted action accuracy by 3.8%
evidence.support_explanation: Run-to-run sampling sensitivity is of the same order as many reported ablation differences.

evidence.quote: We randomly sample 20 failure cases by AutoDroid
evidence.support_explanation: Failure audit covers 20 cases and three causes; no denominator of total failures.

evidence.quote: AutoDroid achieved a precision of 75.0% and a recall of 80.5%.
evidence.support_explanation: Risky-action detection quality (positive class).
Cost of privacy/security gating on 5 apps.

evidence.quote: Although existing research ( Wang et al., 2023 ) attempts to enable LLMs to understand mobile UIs, it simply relies on prompt engineering and does not utilize app-specific domain knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap against the nearest LLM baseline.

evidence.quote: it is usually lengthy (about 40k tokens on average for each UI state) and difficult for LLMs to interpret.
evidence.support_explanation: Quantified representation bottleneck (raw tree).

evidence.quote: relying solely on prompt engineering for LLMs to produce common-sense solutions can result in mistakes.
evidence.support_explanation: Why app knowledge is needed (deep options such as more options then settings).

evidence.quote: LLM-framework ( Wang et al., 2023 ) is an LLM-based framework that enables diverse language-based interactions with mobile UIs.
evidence.support_explanation: Main baseline is a UI-interaction prompting framework, not a multi-step agent loop with memory.

evidence.quote: we can augment smaller LLMs by fine-tuning using app-specific data.
evidence.support_explanation: Vicuna arm is fine-tuned on data derived from the same apps.

evidence.quote: Note that the app and task in the MoTiF dataset ( Burns et al., 2022 ) are unrelated to our dataset.
evidence.support_explanation: Only the MoTiF mixing data is stated to be disjoint.

evidence.quote: AutoDroid first automatically scrolls through all scrollable components and records the information of the visible UI elements
evidence.support_explanation: Scroll handled by the system rather than by the model.

evidence.quote: Increased latency limits the practical use of AutoDroid.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede latency limit.

evidence.quote: Hence, we impose the necessity for LLMs to produce results in a predetermined structure
evidence.support_explanation: Constrained output format (id, action, input text).

Our arithmetic: in the GPT-4 column the completion-judgement accuracy of LLM-framework is 0% while AutoDroid is 93.7%, and Section 6.3 says the completion-rate comparison (Figure 7) leaves the completion-determination step out. The +36.4 point overall action-accuracy gap therefore mixes a real representation/memory effect (click 65.4% to 91.2%, input 27.5% to 82.5%) with a baseline that never emits the completion action; the +39.7 completion-rate gap does not include that step.

Searched main text, Tables 2-5, Discussion and References for: value of k (retrieved simulated tasks), threshold gamma, number of runs/seeds/confidence intervals, held-out apps, comparison of screenshot vs tree input, per-app breakdown. None is reported; Figures 7-9 values are images and not in the extracted text.

signatures.name: Task-oriented UI prompting
signatures.object: Text observation and output interface of the LLM for an Android GUI state (baseline: LLM-framework prompt with visible leaf nodes, ~625 tokens)
signatures.information: Android UI view tree (structural, privileged over pixels); invisible/container nodes pruned; off-screen elements revealed by automatic scrolling; no screenshot used; action history in prompt.
signatures.operation: Convert tree to simplified HTML with 5 tags (button, checkbox, scroller, input, p) carrying id/label/text/value; merge functionally equivalent elements (same UTG edge endpoints, or non-interactive leaves under one clickable ancestor); auto-scroll to include hidden content; force output "id / action / input text" (id=-1 for completion).
signatures.output: One (target element id, action in {tap,input}, text) tuple per step, or task-complete.
signatures.conditions: App exposes a usable view hierarchy; apps are F-Droid utility apps.
signatures.feedback: None beyond history of past actions.
signatures.selection_rule_data: No selection among candidates; the LLM picks one id.
signatures.persistence: None (stateless per step apart from prompt history).
signatures.claimed_effect: Choices per state 36.4 to 13.2; prompt tokens 625.3 to 339.0; on-device latency -21.3%.
signatures.failure_boundary: Multiple valid solutions mis-scored; premature completion; ignoring UI hints; no evidence for canvas/UI-less content.

signatures.name: Exploration-based memory injection
signatures.object: App-specific knowledge supplied to a frozen LLM at inference
signatures.information: Offline stage only: ability to run the app and randomly explore it; LLM summaries of each UI element and UI state; at inference the user task embedding (Instructor-XL) and current UI. Test-task text is not used to build memory.
signatures.operation: Random click exploration -> UI Transition Graph; LLM summarises function of every element -> simulated-task table (task, UI states, UI elements) and UI-function table; at inference retrieve top-k simulated tasks by cosine similarity, and where the current UI matches a stored state add an onclick hint describing what clicking leads to; if similarity exceeds gamma execute the stored action path without calling the LLM (shortcut).
signatures.output: Augmented HTML prompt (onclick hints); optional shortcut action sequence.
signatures.conditions: Same app available offline; random exploration reaches the needed screens; LLM summaries of elements are accurate (unvalidated); k and gamma unspecified in the text.
signatures.feedback: Embedding similarity only; no task-success feedback enters memory construction.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Top-k cosine similarity between simulated task and user task; gamma threshold for shortcuts. No accept/reject based on measured utility.
signatures.persistence: Per-app memory tables stored after a one-off 0.5-1 h exploration + 5-10 min synthesis; read at every later task on that app.
signatures.later_use: Later DroidTask user tasks on the same 13 apps.
signatures.claimed_effect: Completion gains exceed step-accuracy gains (Figure 8, values not extractable); smaller models benefit more; shortcuts correct in 75% of cases and save 38.02% steps when correct.
signatures.failure_boundary: Coverage of random exploration; same-app memory and test; shortcuts misfire 25% of the time.

signatures.name: Reasoning-distilled app-specific fine-tuning of a local LLM
signatures.information: UTG-derived (prompt, correct action) pairs; GPT-4 is shown the correct action and asked to write step-by-step reasoning; a small MoTiF slice supplies input and completion examples.
signatures.operation: Fine-tune Vicuna-7B on (question, zero-shot-CoT answer) pairs generated from the simulated-task table plus the MoTiF slice.
signatures.output: Fine-tuned local model emitting the structured action.
signatures.conditions: Training data is built from the same apps used in the test benchmark.
signatures.feedback: Teacher (GPT-4) rationale conditioned on the known action; no consistency filter.
signatures.selection_rule_data: No filtering reported; MoTiF slice chosen to teach input/complete.
signatures.later_use: DroidTask evaluation on the same apps.
signatures.claimed_effect: Vicuna-7B action accuracy 11.3% to 57.7%, completion 0.6% to 41.1%.
signatures.failure_boundary: With MoTiF but no CoT the model collapses (20.6%); app-specific training/test overlap.

retention_trace.before: Frozen LLM with UI-only prompt and no app knowledge.
retention_trace.proposed_change: Per-app memory tables (simulated tasks, UI functions) built by random exploration + LLM summarisation; optional app-specific fine-tuning of a local LLM.
retention_trace.selection_data_rule: No outcome-based selection; retrieval by embedding similarity at use time; no accept/reject on measured benefit.
retention_trace.persisted_change: App memory files per app; fine-tuned Vicuna weights.
retention_trace.later_tasks: DroidTask user tasks on the same 13 apps.
retention_trace.measured_gain: Qualitative in text for memory (Figure 8 values not extractable); Vicuna fine-tuning 11.3/0.6 to 57.7/41.1 (Table 3).
retention_trace.reason: The paper does not claim self-improvement or a retained-improvement loop; it is a static pipeline with a one-off offline knowledge build. Only the persisted app memory and fine-tuned weights are traced; "retained" in the RSI sense is not claimed.

gap.author_gap: Existing automation needs developer effort or demonstrations/rewards and does not scale; existing LLM approaches rely on prompt engineering and ignore app-specific knowledge; raw UI trees are ~40k tokens; LLM queries are costly.
gap.checked_gap: Real and partly quantified (40k-token trees, Figure 2 navigation example, 625 vs 339 tokens). The headline superiority claim rests on one reproduced baseline (LLM-framework) that differs in representation, scrolling, output format and completion handling, so which of those changes closes the gap is not isolated.

claims.text: Overall: AutoDroid reaches 90.9% action accuracy and 71.3% completion with GPT-4, +36.4 and +39.7 points over GPT-4-powered baselines.
claims.setting: DroidTask: 158 tasks, 13 F-Droid apps; teacher-forced step matching against one human-annotated trace per task; temperature 0.25; GPT-3.5, GPT-4 via API, Vicuna-7B local.
claims.baseline_control: LLM-framework (Wang 2023, reproduced), META-GUI trained on MoTiF, random, embedding-similarity.
claims.selection_vs_test: No dev/test split described; design iteration data not stated. Memory is built from the test apps without using test-task text.
claims.result_denominator: GPT-4 overall action accuracy 54.5% (LLM-F) vs 90.9%; completion +39.7 (value 71.3% in abstract). Step and task denominators not given in extracted text; run count 1 implied.
claims.counterevidence: Baseline scores 0% on the completion action (E006) and the completion comparison excludes that step; multiple valid solution paths are scored wrong (E004); the baseline differs in representation, scrolling, output format and memory simultaneously (E009, E016, E027).
claims.allowed_conclusion: On DroidTask under offline trace matching with GPT-4, the full AutoDroid pipeline scores far above the reproduced LLM-framework baseline. Not supported: live success, unseen apps, attribution of the gain to memory alone.

claims.text: Exploration-based memory injection gives LLMs crucial app knowledge; the completion-rate improvement exceeds the step-accuracy improvement and is larger for smaller models.
claims.setting: Memory on/off for Vicuna-7B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4 on DroidTask (Figure 8).
claims.selection_vs_test: Memory built from same apps; test tasks not used.
claims.result_denominator: Magnitudes are in Figure 8 (not extractable); text only qualitative.
claims.counterevidence: No held-out apps; retrieval precision and accuracy of the LLM summaries not measured.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Memory improves in-app task completion more than step accuracy (author report, magnitude unavailable to us).

claims.text: App-specific CoT-distilled fine-tuning lifts Vicuna-7B from 11.3% to 57.7% action accuracy and 0.6% to 41.1% completion.
claims.setting: Table 3, same benchmark apps; GPT-4 rationales; MoTiF slice for input/complete actions.
claims.baseline_control: Original Vicuna; No Mo; No CoT; No Mo&CoT.
claims.selection_vs_test: Training data derived from the same apps as the test tasks.
claims.counterevidence: CoT hurts badly when MoTiF is added without it (20.6%) yet makes no difference without MoTiF (51.9% both), so the CoT effect is conditional and untested beyond the authors explanation.
claims.allowed_conclusion: App-specific fine-tuning on the evaluation apps raises a 7B model sharply; the contribution of the rationales is not cleanly isolated.

claims.text: Query optimisation cuts prompt tokens by nearly half, per-step on-device latency by 21.3%, LLM calls by 13.7%, and shortcuts save 1.73 steps per task when correct.
claims.setting: Section 6.5, Table 4, five sampled prompts for latency.
claims.result_denominator: Token means over the benchmark (625.3 vs 339.0); latency on 5 prompts; shortcuts correct 75%.
claims.counterevidence: Five-prompt latency sample; 25% shortcut misfires; offline preparation per app 0.5-1 h.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Token and call counts drop measurably relative to the baseline prompt on this benchmark.

assessment.author_claim_preserved: handles arbitrary tasks on any Android app without manual effort; 71.3% success rate
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 158 DroidTask tasks in 13 open-source apps, with exploration performed on those same apps, the AutoDroid prompting + memory pipeline substantially exceeds a reproduced LLM-framework prompt baseline under offline trace-matching metrics, and reduces prompt tokens by about 46%. Live task success, unseen-app transfer and the individual contribution of memory versus representation are not established.

assessment.reproduction: No reproduction was run; all numbers are author reports.

G.reason: Concrete bottleneck with numbers (about 40k-token trees, 625.3-token baseline prompts, Figure 2 deep-navigation example) and a named nearest LLM baseline; the lineage is thin (one reproduced LLM baseline plus META-GUI) and later live-execution residue is not stated, so not 4.

M.reason: Operations map to named obstacles: tree text and pruning for representation, onclick hints from the exploration graph for hidden navigation, shortcuts for cost. The assumptions that random exploration covers the needed screens and that LLM function summaries are correct are left untested, and no distinguishing prediction against a naive memory dump is offered.

X.reason: Pipeline and algorithm are reconstructable (tags, merge rules, algorithm 1, offline costs, fine-tuning recipe), but retrieval k and shortcut gamma are unreported, the completion-action handling in the baseline is unclear, and failure/transfer boundaries (coverage, unseen apps) are not stated.

E.measurement.reason: Scores are offline teacher-forced matches to one annotated trace; the authors acknowledge that alternative valid paths count as errors and decline to report live success. The 71.3% label "success rate" therefore overstates the measurement. Programmatic matching is at least objective and the metric is defined.

E.causality.reason: A memory on/off ablation across three LLMs and a fine-tuning ablation exist, but the headline comparison to the baseline changes representation, scrolling, output constraint, completion handling and memory at once, with the baseline getting 0% on the completion action; the memory effect magnitudes are not recoverable from the text.

E.holdout.reason: Memory and fine-tuning data are built on the same 13 apps used for testing; no unseen apps; benchmark authored by the method authors; only the MoTiF slice is stated disjoint. No test-task text enters memory construction, which avoids direct leakage.

E.statistics.reason: Single run per setting; sampling-temperature sensitivity of 2-4 points is reported by the authors; failure analysis covers 20 sampled failures without total counts; no confidence intervals.

E.cost.reason: Token counts, API cost per 1000 queries, on-device latency, LLM-call reduction, shortcut savings and per-app offline preparation time are all reported with baseline comparisons; latency (only five prompts) and end-to-end cost with GPT-4 across the benchmark are not fully reported.

readable_summary: System method (UI prompting + exploration memory + query optimisation), score 60.0, offline, claim scoped. Clear pipeline and thorough cost reporting; but the 71.3% "success" is offline matching to one annotated trace, memory and fine-tuning use the same 13 test apps, the baseline differs in several ways and scores 0% on the completion action, and there is a single run.
